requirements.title: Establish licensing terms for arbiter
requirements.description: Partly closed by engineering as of 2026-09-14; the remainder needs counsel and cannot be completed here. LICENSE exists at the repository root and pyproject.toml references it, copyright is asserted to Nicholas J Pauken, and LICENSE section 3 assigns scan output to the user -- the first three acceptance criteria. LICENSE is explicitly an interim notice and not the operative grant: it reserves all rights and grants none. The fourth criterion is L-6, the redistribution review for the five bundled analyzers, recorded in NOTICE.md with a date and a named reviewer. That is a legal determination about semgrep's LGPL-2.1 terms and it must not be signed by anyone who did not perform it, so this requirement stays pending until a person does. It blocks the air-gapped bundle and nothing else; docs/licensing.md records the open questions.
acceptance_criteria: a LICENSE file exists at the repository root and pyproject.toml references it
copyright ownership is asserted
ownership of scan output is assigned to the user
the redistribution review for bundled analyzers is recorded in NOTICE.md with a date and a reviewer
risk_notes: Requires qualified legal review and cannot be completed by engineering alone
the air-gapped bundle roadmap item stays blocked until the semgrep LGPL-2.1 redistribution question is answered
2026-10-09: the air-gapped bundle now ships without the analyzers (ARB-051); only including them in the bundle stays blocked on the L-6 redistribution review.

requirements.title: Attribute every adjudication verdict to a reviewer and a time
requirements.description: learn.record() stores a verdict as the bare string 'true_positive' or 'false_positive:note' in Knowledge.adjudicated, with no reviewer, no per-verdict timestamp and no record of which entry point it arrived through. Only the rule carries first_seen/last_seen. The ledger refuses re-adjudication, so a wrong or machine-written mark is permanent and, today, untraceable: there is no way to find whose marks to distrust. The rule that verdicts come from a person is enforced in assistant instructions, not in the code. This matters more now that agents hold shell access and more again if a second person ever adjudicates.
acceptance_criteria: Knowledge.adjudicated holds a structured record carrying verdict reviewer timestamp and entry point rather than a bare string/KNOWLEDGE_VERSION is raised and from_dict migrates a version 1 ledger without losing any existing verdict/record() requires a reviewer identity and refuses to write without one/the reviewer is resolved from an explicit flag or git config user rather than defaulted silently/a test asserts a version 1 ledger round-trips through the new schema/a test asserts a verdict without a reviewer is refused
risk_notes: The ledger is committed and feeds version_hash() so the schema change moves the knowledge version and any pinned scan must be re-pinned/The live ledger has zero adjudications so migration is untested against real data and should be tested against a synthetic version 1 file/Attribution records who not whether they were human and must not be described as proof of personhood

requirements.title: Refuse an adjudication verdict from a non-interactive session
requirements.description: Nothing distinguishes a verdict typed by a person from one written by a script or an agent. review_ui._getch() falls back to input() when raw terminal mode is unavailable, nothing calls isatty(), and cli.cmd_feedback records a verdict from a fully non-interactive invocation. review --apply reads marks from a markdown file, so anything that can write markdown can adjudicate. This is no barrier against a determined caller and is not claimed to be one; it stops the accidental case, which is a piped script, a CI job or an agent shelling out.
acceptance_criteria: the interactive adjudication paths require stdin to be a terminal and refuse otherwise with a reason/the refusal names an explicit override flag so a deliberate batch import is possible and visible/an overridden verdict is recorded with an entry point that says it was not interactive/docs/calibration.md states plainly that this is a guard against accident and not proof of personhood/a test asserts a piped non-interactive feedback invocation is refused
risk_notes: Depends on ARB-020 for the entry point field so it should land after it/An override flag that is easy to pass is an override an agent can pass so the value is the record it leaves not the obstacle it creates/Existing tests that record verdicts programmatically will need the override or a direct call to record()

requirements.title: Declare adapter probe scope deliberately and say what a partial scan does not run
requirements.description: adapters.register_adapters constructs every adapter-backed Probe without a scope argument, so all five external analyzers inherit the repo default from Probe and are recorded as not-assessed in any partial scan. The default is right because nothing has established that ruff bandit checkov semgrep or gitleaks give subset-exact answers on a file subset, but it is inherited rather than chosen. docs/ci.md explains file and repo scope carefully and never names the external analyzers; RUNNING-ON-YOUR-OWN-CODE.md describes the pull-request job without saying it runs native probes only. A reader of either document would reasonably believe their gate runs semgrep. It does not.
acceptance_criteria: every adapter manifest declares its scope explicitly/register_adapters passes the declared scope instead of relying on the Probe default/docs/ci.md names the five external analyzers as repo-scoped and says a partial scan does not run them/RUNNING-ON-YOUR-OWN-CODE.md says the same where it describes the pull-request job/a test asserts no adapter-backed probe relies on the inherited default

requirements.description: The nightly calibration job in .github/workflows/train.yml and tools/train_cycle.sh has never been covered by a requirement. Four defects were repaired in it on 2026-09-13 as unplanned work, including one where git add matched a gitignore entry, git exited 1, and bash -e failed the job two seconds after a 55-minute cycle finished successfully, so run 1 measured everything and committed nothing. A job that produces the project's only accumulating evidence and can fail silently after doing all its work needs owned acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: Exercise the Windows code paths in CI
requirements.description: Originally: no workflow ran on Windows, so no Windows path was ever exercised by automation. ARB-006 fixed a crash that occurred on every adapter timeout on Windows and it survived to be found by hand because nothing tested it. pr-check.yml is a matrix over ubuntu-latest and windows-latest with fail-fast false and no continue-on-error, running the suite with -rs so each platform's skips appear with reasons, then tools/integrity.py and tools/mutate_tests.py, omni doctor and omni gate, and on Linux the analyzers and arbiter's own gate. Seven tests were added; four of them delete os.killpg so the taskkill fallback is exercised on Linux too. The matrix ran for the first time on 2026-10-09 (PR #3) and found two real defects (FAIL-035, FAIL-039). The last criterion, making the check required rather than advisory, was decided against on 2026-10-09: a required check only blocks the merge button, which a sole committer already reads, and the strict variant would make every pull request stale after each nightly training commit. Revisit when a second committer or automated merging arrives.

requirements.title: Stop vendored and generated content from being scanned as first-party source
requirements.description: Scanning STEP-Migration and STEP_App as a system surfaced three compounding gaps that together reported a third-party library's own source as a leaked private key, and buried real findings under tens of thousands from vendored code. (1) _pem_has_key_material judged a PEM block real by checking whether any text after a BEGIN marker contained a colon anywhere in the next ~4000 characters -- a check meant to allow encrypted-key preambles (Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED), but satisfied by almost any surrounding prose or code, so ecdsa's own PEM-parsing source and packaging metadata were reported as committed keys. (2) inventory.classify()'s GENERATED_HINTS/IAC_HINTS hardcoded the literal name cdk.out, so a project using CDK_OUTDIR to redirect synth output to a renamed directory (cdk.out.chk, seen on the real system) fell through to role=source, and a branch-ordering bug meant that even the unrenamed case would have classified a CDK stack's own synthesized *.template.json as generated rather than the iac role that exempts nothing, losing the ground-truth scanning SKIP_DIRS says is deliberate. (3) bandit and checkov each walk {workdir} with their own traversal, independent of SKIP_DIRS, so both walked into a full vendored .venv and a Lambda asset bundle's dependencies regardless of role -- bandit alone produced 129,379 raw findings and consumed 669s of its 900s budget on one such tree.
acceptance_criteria: _pem_has_key_material walks forward line by line and stops at the first line that is not base64 or a Key: value header
so surrounding code or prose cannot manufacture a body
classify() recognises a CDK_OUTDIR-renamed cdk.out* directory and classifies its synthesized *.template.json as iac rather than letting the directory-wide generated match swallow it
bandit and checkov are invoked with exclusions mirroring inventory.SKIP_DIRS plus a CDK asset-bundle pattern
verified empirically against a real vendored tree rather than assumed from documentation
validation_required: python -m pytest tests/ -q is 421 passed 3 skipped 0 failed
a real cross-repo scan of STEP-Migration + STEP_App dropped from 3 critical / 6011 total findings to 0 critical / 1121 total
with 0 findings remaining inside a vendored asset bundle and bandit's runtime dropping from 669s to 4s
risk_notes: the bandit/checkov exclude patterns are a fixed list mirroring SKIP_DIRS rather than reading it programmatically
so the two lists can drift apart if SKIP_DIRS changes without the adapters being updated to match

requirements.title: Fix adapter output paths and scan scope that broke on Windows and outside the fixture corpus
requirements.description: Four related gaps surfaced by continuing ARB-026's cross-repo scanning work. (1) gitleaks has no write-JSON-to-stdout mode; --report-path took the conventional '-' literally, creating a file named '-' inside {workdir} (the repo being scanned, since the adapter never set cwd) full of gitleaks' own JSON output -- itself full of strings shaped like the secrets it exists to find -- for the next scan of any repo to read as content. Adapter.invoke() now substitutes a private temp path for a '{report_file}' placeholder, reads it back after the process exits, and deletes it in a finally block. (2) checkov and bandit hand back backslash-separated relative paths on Windows -- checkov's own output even starts with a bare leading backslash -- but every suppress-rule glob and Location.path in this codebase assumes '/', so path-based rules silently matched zero Windows findings from either tool; Adapter now normalizes backslashes to '/' before the existing './' stripping. (3) ARB-026 gave bandit and checkov exclusions mirroring inventory.SKIP_DIRS but flagged in its own risk_notes that semgrep, which walks {workdir} with its own traversal same as the other two, was not covered; semgrep.adapter.toml now carries the same --exclude list plus a cdk.out* pattern, for the same reason as bandit: none of its configured rulesets understand CloudFormation templates. (4) SKIP_DIRS is a fixed name list and can never cover a fresh arbiter-out/ (or any other untracked, .gitignore-matched directory) left over from a previous run under whatever --out name was given that time; walk_repo now also excludes whatever git itself calls untracked-and-ignored via 'git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory', which is the same plumbing incremental.py already uses for changed-file detection.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter.invoke substitutes {report_file} with a private temp path for tools that require a real output filename
reads it back
and always deletes it

requirements.title: Test the scanner against reformulations of its own input, and test the measurement code
requirements.description: An audit of every testing parameter and the whole bug history found nineteen shipped defects collapsing into five recurring root causes, each previously fixed with a fixture for the one case that failed: platform and path assumptions, encoding defaults, attribution propagation, heuristic proxies with unhandled edges, and bugs in the measurement code itself. Three live defects were found by the audit. (1) Finding.fingerprint() hashed location.path unnormalized, so the same finding had different identities on Windows and Linux; because adjudications are permanent and keyed by fingerprint, a verdict recorded on one platform could never match the other, and a baseline built on one reported everything as new on the other. Normalization moved to the Location boundary that all ~54 construction sites pass through. (2) tools/calibrate_external.py wrote measured severities to a report file while learn.apply() read a map inside knowledge.json, with no code path between them -- every nightly measurement of the external tools had been changing nothing, and the live map came from a one-off step that no longer exists. (3) calibrate_external.py documented a >=50x -> high band its own BANDS constant cannot produce. Two further defects were found by the new tests: seven config reads used the platform default codec, which on Windows mis-decodes silently rather than raising; and inventory._is_binary treated any NUL byte as binary, so every UTF-16 file was classified as data and never read at all.

no finding from any fixture scan carries a backslash absolute or escaping path
every finding in a multi-repo scan names a repository that exists
every text read and write under src names an explicit encoding

so they cover Arbiter's reading of code and not whether a rule's judgement matches a person's; that gap is the empty adjudicated ledger and only a reviewer can close it

requirements.title: Probe precision on real repositories: history-aware doc drift, prose excluded from suppression scanning, a house rule that means what it says, tooling attributed upstream, and not-applicable probes kept out of the coverage denominator
requirements.description: The self-scan's noise had five distinct causes. drift.doc-references-missing-file reported 24 paths named in CHANGELOG.md and project-context.md, most of them files that once existed and were deliberately removed or renamed, which an append-only history file is right to mention; the probe now asks git whether the path was ever tracked and reports those at info as removed rather than missing. assurance.blanket-suppression fired on Markdown prose that discusses # noqa; the probe now skips the docs role. house/no-bare-except matched every except clause, including except OSError, because its tree-sitter query had no predicate; it now matches only bare and Exception/BaseException clauses. OmniEngineering's own make_ai.py, omni_graph.py and omni_mcp.py were scored as arbiter's code in the quality dimension (44 of 90 complexity findings); arbiter.yaml now suppresses quality findings on them with the reason recorded, so they stay visible and attributed. The interface probe on a single-repository scan reported skipped with 0% dimension coverage although there is nothing to assess; a probe that declares itself not applicable is now recorded as such and excluded from the coverage denominator, while a probe that could have run but did not still counts against coverage.

requirements.title: Full scans are faster: adapters run concurrently and replay when nothing they read changed

requirements.title: The governance probe tags a finding with the requirements its file's recent commits cite, not every open one
requirements.description: req: tags named every open requirement, so a finding in a gate run cited all five requirements of a round and OmniEngineering's graph could not say which one introduced it. The probe now reads the commits between the gate base (changed_since) and HEAD that touch the finding's path, collects the requirement ids their messages cite (through the registry's aliases), and tags those as req:; only when none cites one does it fall back to the open requirements, adding a req-scope:open tag so a reader knows the tags are context rather than attribution. A full scan without a base keeps today's behaviour with the same marker.
